root_cause.text: The length argument passed to rtw_update_protection() was not reduced to reflect the pointer offset into the IEs buffer, causing the function to read beyond the valid buffer when the IE length is smaller than the fixed IE header size.
root_cause.evidence: The patch subtracts sizeof(struct ndis_802_11_fix_ie) from the length in both call sites (update_current_network and rtw_joinbss_update_network) and adds a guard check to ensure ie_length >= sizeof(struct ndis_802_11_fix_ie) before the subtraction. The commit description directly states the cause: "called with a pointer offset into the ies buffer but the full ie_length is passed, causing a potential buffer over-read."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential buffer underflow and incorrect length calculation when updating network protection.
intent_record.what: Added a guard condition that returns early if ie_length is less than sizeof(struct ndis_802_11_fix_ie); changed the length argument in rtw_update_protection from ie_length to ie_length - sizeof(struct ndis_802_11_fix_ie).
intent_record.how: Prevents calling rtw_update_protection with a too-short buffer and corrects the length to exclude the fixed IE header, avoiding out-of-bounds memory access and ensuring the function receives the correct remaining length.
